subject: SLO measurement, visibility, and exception flow for Nimbus Health
messages:
From: Sarah Long <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:08:00 -0800
Subject: SLO measurement / monitoring / exception process (procurement questionnaire)

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Nimbus Health is putting together the procurement packet and we have a few detailed questions about how Redwood measures and exposes SLOs, and the process for requesting exceptions. Our Security and SRE teams need answers for the vendor review. High level questions below; we can follow up on a short call if easier.

1) Measurement definitions
- Do you define availability as successful inference responses (2xx) over total requests, or do you measure by user-facing completion? Which status codes count as failures?
- Which latency buckets do you publish by default (p50/p95/p99)? Can we request a custom percentile?
- What sampling window is used for SLO calculations (rolling 30d, 7d)? Is there an option for monthly aggregation?

2) Monitoring & access
- What metrics are available to customers via the console/Grafana (per-route latency, error_rate, throughput, queueing)?
- Can we get a read-only Grafana view scoped to our account and specific model routes? What is the invitation workflow and TTL for that token?
- Retention: what are the default retention periods for raw telemetry, aggregated SLOs, and traces? Is export (CSV/JSON) supported?

3) Alerts & escalations
- Do you provide alerting templates for breach (e.g., sustained p95 > X ms for 10m)? Are alert hooks supported (PagerDuty, Webhook, Email)?
- Can alerts be scoped per-model or per-environment (prod/staging)?

4) Exception request process
- If we anticipate not meeting a latency SLO during a planned migration, what is the formal exception request path? Typical timelines? Required mitigations and reporting cadence?

5) Evidence artifacts
- Do you provide an SLO playbook or runbook, service-level telemetry export, and recent uptime reports we can share with Procurement?

If you can send a short playbook or the specific document we should attach to our packet that would be ideal. Also, if you can include a sample Grafana invite (or steps to request one) that would speed the review.

Thanks,
Sarah Long
Senior Procurement Manager | Nimbus Health
procurement@nimbushealth.com

P.S. I copied Michael Chen from Ops — he may add technical follow-ups on thresholds and retention.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: SLO measurement / monitoring / exception process (procurement questionnaire)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and attached is our SLO Telemetry Playbook (redwood_slo_telemetry_playbook.pdf) that has examples and templates you can drop into your procurement packet. Also attached is a small text file with the Grafana invite flow (grafana-readonly-invite.txt).

Summary answers (short):
- Availability: we measure request-level success (2xx) over total requests by default; configurable to treat specific model responses as failures if customers have special business logic.
- Latency percentiles: p50, p95, p99 are standard; we can add a custom percentile on request (engineering lead sign-off). Standard SLO windows are rolling 30d for contractual SLOs and shorter 7d windows for operational alerts; monthly aggregates are exportable.
- Monitoring access: customers get per-route dashboards (latency, error_rate, qps, queue_time). Read-only Grafana access is supported via an invite token; tokens are one-time redeemable and you control which teams/roles are granted access.
- Retention: default raw telemetry = 90 days, aggregated SLO buckets = 13 months, traces = 30 days (longer retention available as an add-on). Exports supported via Console -> Exports (CSV/JSON) and API.
- Alerts: built-in templates (threshold and rolling-window based) and integrations for PagerDuty, OpsGenie, Slack, and webhooks. Alerts can be scoped by model route and by deployment tag (prod/staging).
- Exception requests: formal process is in the attached playbook (section 4). Typical path: exception request form -> engineering review -> mitigation plan & weekly reporting -> approval with expiry (usually 30–90 days). We require an agreed mitigation (e.g., autoscale bump, controlled rollout, temporary SLA credit) and weekly telemetry snapshots while exception is active.

Next steps:
1) We can schedule a 30m call this week with Karhtik (serving/runtime lead) and Laura (Customer Success) to review the exception template and invite the Ops team to Grafana.
2) Please confirm the two Ops contacts you want invited and the window you anticipate for any exception (if already known).

Attaching: redwood_slo_telemetry_playbook.pdf, grafana-readonly-invite.txt

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 6:34 PM Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and attached is our SLO Telemetry Playbook...

Sarah — small technical addendum from the runtime side. We frequently see customers request a short-term latency SLO exception during initial rollout or prefix/cache integration. We can support a planned exception but we request the following to approve and operationalize it: 

- Exception window: indicate intended start/end dates (we typically approve 30–90 days).
- Mitigations: list concrete mitigations (e.g., increase reserved capacity, enable continuous batching, add prefix caching, circuit-breaker rules).
- Reporting cadence: weekly telemetry export (we will provide a CSV with p50/p95/p99 by route and error breakdown) and a short summary note.
- Stop-gap SLA credit: optional, discussed on a case-by-case basis for severe breaches.

If you include those elements in the exception form in the playbook we can move to an engineering review within 3 business days. For very latency-sensitive flows we sometimes propose a canary window (split traffic) as a less disruptive alternative.

Finally, regarding access: please list the Ops personnel and their email addresses. We can issue a read-only Grafana invite that scopes to your account and masks other tenants. Invite TTLs are configurable (we typically issue 30-day tokens for procurement review).

— Karthik
Sr. Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood_slo_telemetry_playbook.pdf
